# 5 Tips for Naming an AI Startup When the .ai Domain You Want Is Taken


By OpenTools Team


·


November 23, 2026


Finding the proper name for an AI startup is surprisingly hard. You could spend days trying to come up with something that sounds good, just to find out that another organization has already registered the same .ai domain. There are a lot of companies entering the AI field, therefore, short and recognized names can be hard to come by.


The good news is, if a domain name isn’t accessible, it doesn’t mean you have to give up on the corporate branding you want. Founders can check out other names, domain extensions and registration deals. A[Hostinger domain coupon](https://hostadvice.com/hosting-company/hostinger-coupons/hostinger-domain-coupon/) can also help lower the cost of eligible registrations. Before you buy another address, consider how the name you want will grow with your company.


1. **Catchy Short Name**


A startup name should be easy to spell, say and remember. When they hear the name in discussions or presentations, clients may become confused by complicated words or odd combinations. If your favorite domain isn’t accessible, try reducing the name or combining two relevant words. Don't try to use random numbers or extra punctuation to get an available address. A simple, identifiable brand will be easier to utilize on websites, ads and social media.


1. **Use Different Domain Extensions**


Most people will think of the .ai domain as something for AI companies but it’s not a must for an AI startup. Extensions like .com, .io or .tech can also work depending on your target. Consider how the option meshes with your brand and how your customers would view it. Some extensions can be a lot more expensive than others so check out registration and renewal prices before you commit. Since your organization is still establishing itself, a cheaper domain name may be fine.


1. **Add a Related Word to Your Brand Name**


If you can’t get the exact domain, try to add a short word describing your product or service. When a company builds an AI writing program, they might include terminology that relates to content. If a company builds[automation tools](https://www.microsoft.com/en/power-platform/products/power-automate/topics/workflow-automation/workflow-automation-software-and-tools) , it might include phrases related to processes. Additions should flow naturally and relate to the objective of the company. Overly descriptive names can prove limiting if the business subsequently extends to new services. Try a few combinations before making a decision.


1. **Check Trademark and Social Media Availability**


Even if a domain is available, a business name may not be safe. Some competitors may have a trademark on similar wording. Look up trademark databases. Find companies in the sector. The[USPTO](https://www.uspto.gov/) makes available to the public searches of registered and pending trademarks. Get the best social media sites. Tags are optional, but consistent user names will make for a noticeable startup.


1. **Check Prices of Domains Before You Register**


Prices for domain registration vary by provider, extension and promotion. Introductory incentives may lower your rate the first term but increase your renewal rate. Check the prices before selecting an offer based on its advertised price. Read the privacy and registration terms. Secure your account settings. If your startup name is part of your brand, file it before you start it.


**Pick a Name That Can Grow With Your Startup**


The .ai domain might not be available. Consider alternative naming options. Choose a name that will appeal to customers and reflect your long‑term vision. Check the legal status, registration costs and how it can be used in practice on digital platforms. A deliberate decision can help to set a consistent identity as your AI startup grows.
